record.paper_title: Ball-Evans approximation problem: recent progress and open problems
record.original_question: Let n ≥ 4 and 1 ≤ p < floor(n/2). Is it possible to construct a homeomorphism f ∈ W^{1,p}(B(0,R), B(0,R)) such that f(x) = x on the boundary ∂B(0,R) and Jf < 0 almost everywhere in [0,1]^n?

evidence.quote: Open problem 10. Can we have Jf < 0 a.e. for all p < [n/2]: Let n ≥ 4 and 1 ≤ p < [n/2]. Is it possible to construct a homeomorphism f ∈ W1,p(B(0, R), B(0, R)) such that f(x) = x for x ∈ ∂B(0, R) and Jf < 0 a.e. in [0, 1]^n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 4$ be an integer and let $p$ be a real number with $1 \leq p < \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. Fix $R > 0$ and let $B(0,R) \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ denote the open Euclidean ball of radius $R$ centred at the origin, chosen so that $[0,1]^n \subset B(0,R)$. For a mapping $f: B(0,R) \to \mathbb{R}^n$ in the Sobolev space $W^{1,p}(B(0,R),\mathbb{R}^n)$, write $J_f(x) = \det Df(x)$ for the Jacobian determinant of its weak derivative.

Determine whether there exists a homeomorphism $f \in W^{1,p}(B(0,R), B(0,R))$ such that:
(i) $f(x) = x$ for every $x \in \partial B(0,R)$, and
(ii) $J_f(x) < 0$ for almost every $x \in [0,1]^n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is part of a recent line of research on the sign of the Jacobian of Sobolev homeomorphisms. For $n=2,3$ (any $p\geq 1$) or $n\geq 4$ with $p>\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, the Jacobian of a Sobolev homeomorphism cannot change sign. Campbell (J. London Math. Soc., 2022) constructed a sense-preserving Sobolev homeomorphism with negative Jacobian a.e. for low integrability exponents, and partial results exist for $n\geq 4$, $p<\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ (mixed-sign Jacobians on sets of positive measure). However, the specific problem of producing a homeomorphism in $W^{1,p}$ for the full range $1\leq p<\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ that equals the identity on $\partial B(0,R)$ and satisfies $J_f<0$ a.e. on $[0,1]^n$ appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A sense-preserving Sobolev homeomorphism with negative Jacobian almost everywhere
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a Sobolev homeomorphism equal to identity on the boundary of a cube with negative Jacobian almost everywhere.
status_evidence.claim: Related construction exists in some regimes; addresses partial cases of the Hajłasz problem.

status_evidence.title: Jacobians of W^{1,p} homeomorphisms, case p=[n/2]
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the borderline case p=[n/2] for Jacobians of Sobolev homeomorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Sign-change phenomena occur only for p<[n/2] when n>=4; the borderline and lower-exponent cases have been studied but the precise problem remains.
